changes.comment: A delivered document comment now says what it is about. Three attributes join the envelope: `anchor`, which is `whole_document` or `content` and is absent exactly when the comment could not be read — so a comment the commenter put on the whole document is no longer indistinguishable from one with no text; `anchor_id`, Feishu's id for the anchored content, which for a docx is the block id lark-cli reads back in full; and `anchor_deleted`, written only when Feishu says the anchored content is gone. The `<quote>` block is unchanged in shape but no longer described as the document text the comment is anchored to: its note now says it is a preview Feishu shortens, and points at `anchor_id` for the content itself. The channel fetches no anchored content of its own — one anchored part can be far larger than every comment on it, and the recipient decides whether it wants the passage. A delivered comment is also logged for what it was. The log said "delivered" for every outcome but a proven rejection, which hid a comment refused because the session had closed and a body Core would not admit; it now reports what Core answered — admitted, not admitted, rejected before admission, ambiguous, or failed — at the severity each earns. Both delivery paths read that classification from one place beside the outcome type instead of each keeping its own, because they had already drifted apart on it; each keeps only its own wording. The chat path's log lines are unchanged except that its failure lines now also carry the outcome's `status`.
